reason: E2 supports the formation of a protective oxide layer and increased wear resistance at elevated temperature for the specified alloy and processing route, but provides no evidence for oxide disruption, healing failure, or synergistic wear-corrosion mechanisms. E1 discusses galvanic corrosion and passive film breakdown in a different HEA system (CoCrFeNiMo) under static conditions, not under simultaneous wear, and does not address the proposed mechanism. The key premises about mechanical disruption, healing prevention, and synergistic degradation are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 HEA produced via powder metallurgy/SPS forms a protective oxide film at elevated temperatures
Mechanical abrasion disrupts this protective oxide film
Disrupted oxide film cannot heal, exposing reactive metal surfaces
Exposed surfaces undergo aggressive localized corrosion
Corrosion weakens the material, accelerating wear (synergistic degradation)
